# mgc_tag (Resource)

A tag that can be attached to cloud resources, to organize and report on them. Tags are global: they are not bound to a region. Attaching a tag to a resource also requires a value (`mgc_tag_value`) and an attachment (`mgc_tag_attachment`).

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "mgc_tag" "ambiente" {
  name        = "ambiente"
  description = "Separa os recursos por ambiente"
  color       = "0086ff"
  kinds       = ["finops"]
}
```

## Renaming or Deleting a Tag in Use

The API has no rename. Changing `name` makes Terraform destroy the tag and create
a new one, and destroying a tag that is still attached to a resource fails with a
`409 Conflict`.

Terraform cannot avoid this on its own. A `mgc_tag_attachment` that only changes
its `tags` map is updated in place, never replaced, so it has no destroy step that
Terraform could schedule before the tag goes away. Its update also depends on the
new tag existing, which puts it last. The order Terraform picks is: destroy the old
value, destroy the old tag, create the new tag, create the new value, update the
attachment — and the first step already fails.

### `create_before_destroy`

Invert the default order with the
[`create_before_destroy` meta argument](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle#create_before_destroy)
on both the tag and its values. The new pair is created first, the attachment is
updated to point at it, and only then is the old pair destroyed. The tagged
resource is never left without its tag:

```terraform
resource "mgc_tag" "ambiente" {
  name = "ambiente"

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

resource "mgc_tag_value" "producao" {
  tag_name = mgc_tag.ambiente.name
  name     = "producao"

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

### `replace_triggered_by`

An alternative that leaves the tag and the value untouched is to force the
attachment to be replaced along with the tag, using the
[`replace_triggered_by` meta argument](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/meta-arguments/lifecycle#replace_triggered_by).
The attachment then has a destroy step, which Terraform runs before destroying the
tag. Note that this leaves the resource briefly without any tag, between the
destruction of the old attachment and the creation of the new one:

```terraform
resource "mgc_tag_attachment" "vpc" {
  resource_id = mgc_network_vpcs.main.id

  tags = {
    (mgc_tag.ambiente.name) = mgc_tag_value.producao.name
  }

  lifecycle {
    replace_triggered_by = [mgc_tag.ambiente]
  }
}
```

### Conflicts Outside a Rename

A `409 Conflict` on a plain destroy, with no rename involved, means the tag is
attached to a resource that this configuration does not manage. The
`mgc_tag_attachments` data source lists every tagged resource of the tenant, which
is where to look for it. It has to be detached before the tag can be destroyed.

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the tag, unique within the tenant. Names are case sensitive: `finops` and `FinOps` are different tags. The API has no rename, so changing this replaces the tag. While the tag is attached to a resource that replacement fails with a conflict, unless `create_before_destroy` is set on this resource and on its `mgc_tag_value` resources.

### Optional

- `color` (String) Color of the tag, as a 6-digit hex RGB code without the `#` prefix. Case insensitive: the API stores it lowercased. When omitted, the API assigns a color, which is why this value is kept in state. The API has no way to clear a color, so removing this from the configuration keeps the current one.
- `description` (String) A brief description of the tag.
- `kinds` (Set of String) Kinds that describe what the tag is for, such as `finops`.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Creation date of the tag.
- `id` (String) The tag name, which is also its identifier.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update date of the tag, null while it was never updated.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Tags are imported by name, which is also their id.
terraform import mgc_tag.ambiente ambiente
```
